page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.medium is a general-purpose instance powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. This single-core, single-threaded arm64 server features 4.0 GB of system memory and includes a bundled 59 GB NVMe SSD local instance store volume. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1735.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1693.28. Single-threaded tasks like bzip3 decompression show strong performance at 14.02 GB/sec, while gzip compression performs at an average rate of 30.03 GB/sec. However, due to its single-core configuration, multi-core benchmarks are poor, matching the single-core results. Memory bandwidth is limited, with large-block read and write speeds categorized as weak and poor respectively.

The primary tradeoff of the m8gd.medium is its single-core limitation, which restricts its utility for parallel processing, software compilation, or heavy multi-threaded workloads. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, single-threaded applications requiring fast local NVMe storage. Suitable workloads include basic web serving, simple database operations, text processing, and lightweight background tasks that do not require high network throughput or multi-core execution.
